thesisQuality.note: Long-duration hyperscaler commitments and >1 GW contracted capacity support an AI-infrastructure thesis; leverage and delivery risk cap conviction.

financialOperatingMomentum.note: FY2026 revenue reached $611.3M and Q4 revenue $258.7M, up 407% YoY, with positive adjusted EBITDA, while GAAP losses remain material.

marketValuationOpportunity.note: Sep. 17 market cap about $7.69B and EV about $11.20B against $611.3M FY revenue imply a high current revenue multiple despite growth.

catalystScore.note: Campus delivery and conversion of >1 GW contracted capacity into operating rent provide identifiable execution catalysts.

governancePower.note: Public-company governance is established, but rapid financing and 36.8% YoY share-count growth require conservative capital-allocation treatment.

alignment2036.note: Grid-connected high-density data-center capacity is a direct enabling layer for AI compute expansion.

crossDivisionLeverage.note: Hosting, HPC infrastructure and fit-out capabilities provide multiple monetization paths, though economics remain concentrated in infrastructure delivery.

bottleneckControl.note: Scarce power-dense, grid-connected campuses address a real AI infrastructure bottleneck, but utilities, developers and competing campuses can substitute over time.

scenarioRobustness.note: Long take-or-pay contracts improve demand visibility, offset by construction, financing, tenant and power-delivery concentration.

substitutionResilience.note: Long leases and site-specific power interconnection create switching friction, but competing data-center capacity remains a credible substitute.

supplyChainResilience.note: Large liquidity supports buildout, while power equipment, utility interconnects and construction dependencies remain significant.

pricingPower.note: Long-duration hyperscaler commitments support contracted economics, but disclosed evidence does not establish broad repricing power across tenants.

risk.note: Material leverage, continued GAAP losses, construction/utility execution, tenant concentration, dilution and high-beta valuation risk.

confidence.note: Current issuer operating/contract evidence plus independent current valuation and share-count evidence; tenant/project economics remain explicit non-gating unknowns.

thesis: Applied Digital is converting scarce grid-connected, power-dense campuses into long-duration AI infrastructure contracts, with rapid revenue scaling and substantial contracted demand visibility.
keyRisk: High leverage and capital intensity make construction, utility delivery, tenant concentration and dilution capable of overwhelming strong contracted demand.
nextCatalyst: Next earnings and campus-delivery milestones converting contracted capacity into recurring rent.
